svg.aria-label: Estrogen, progesterone and the menstrual cycle. The hypothalamus releases GnRH; the anterior pituitary releases FSH, which grows ovarian follicles and causes estrogen release; estrogen prompts an LH surge, which causes ovulation. The ruptured follicle becomes the corpus luteum, which produces progesterone. High estrogen plus progesterone suppress FSH and LH and thicken the endometrium. With implantation, HCG maintains the corpus luteum, peaking at 8 to 10 weeks; then the placenta takes over progesterone production. Without implantation, the corpus luteum degenerates, hormones fall and menstruation occurs. Notes cover estradiol, estriol, and post-menopausal FSH and LH.
